title: NTT Leverages Vertiv AC and DC Power Systems to Achieve NTT OneVision Center
summary: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today shared details of the Vertiv™ equipment and services supporting sustainable operation of the NTT OneVision Center, a state-of-the-art hybrid-remote smart workspace for NTT Research, and other NTT Group companies, in Sunnyvale, Calif.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [May 11, 2022] – Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today shared details of the Vertiv™ equipment and services supporting sustainable operation of the NTT OneVision Center, a state-of-the-art hybrid-remote smart workspace for NTT Research, and other NTT Group companies, in Sunnyvale, Calif. A Vertiv™ Liebert® EXM 100 kVA uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system with lithium-ion batteries provides backup power to the building’s IT equipment and other critical systems, and a Vertiv™ NetSure™ outdoor DC power enclosure with inverters, rectifiers and maximum power point tracking (MPPT) solar converters supports solar power implementation. A concept led by NTT Global Sourcing, the NTT OneVision Center is one of the first office buildings in Silicon Valley built specifically with the post-pandemic workplace in mind, prioritizing health and wellness, remote and on-site collaboration, energy efficiency and net-zero carbon emissions. The building is on track to become carbon neutral, thanks to on-site solar energy generation. Vertiv’s technologies and services contribute to the sustainability of the building, through the efficiency of the Liebert EXM UPS, charging and discharging properties of lithium-ion batteries, and by facilitating the use of solar power throughout the building with the NetSure outdoor DC power enclosure and inverters. Vertiv™ Services, including scheduled maintenance, will support the operation and availability of the systems. “Everything about the NTT OneVision Center is about the future of work, and Vertiv helps make it all possible with intelligent, efficient solutions that empower our teams to collaborate and explore their creativity in ways that meet this moment,” said NTT Research president and CEO Kazuhiro Gomi. “We have confidence in Vertiv and their solutions supporting our power infrastructure. We are proud to be leaders in moving toward a smarter, healthier workplace, and we are thrilled to partner with Vertiv to make it happen.” “As NTT Services developed this workspace concept, Vertiv’s comprehensive AC and DC infrastructure support portfolio and their reputation for excellence made them the clear choice to support NTT critical systems and Net Zero energy goals,” said Arvind Kumar, vice president at NTT Global Sourcing. “The vision for the NTT OneVision Center aligns with everything Vertiv is about,” said Peter Panfil, vice president, global power at Vertiv. “Sustainability, intelligence, and enhanced communication and collaboration are expectations in the work we do and in the solutions we deliver for our customers. The NTT Research vision to deliver cutting-edge technologies to enable a smarter, more sustainable and healthier workplace aligns perfectly with Vertiv’s goals.” The Vertiv™ Liebert® EXM 100 kVA is a transformer-free, double-conversion UPS system with a small footprint, modular design and a unity power factor that delivers excellent power per square foot. It is up to 97% efficient in standard operating mode and up to 99% efficient in Eco Mode. The Vertiv™ NetSure™ DC power system works with the inverter to efficiently convert DC power from the building’s solar panels for distribution throughout the building, including to the AC-powered IT systems. NTT Research officially unveiled the NTT OneVision Center in late September 2021. The building is open, but currently accessible only to a limited number of employees. About Vertiv Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, USA, Vertiv employs approximately 24,000 people and does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . Forward-Looking Statements This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, Section 27 of the Securities Act, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act. These statements are only a prediction. Actual events or results may differ materially from those in the forward-looking statement set forth herein. Readers are referred to Vertiv’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including its most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K and any subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for a discussion of these and other important risk factors concerning Vertiv and its operations. Vertiv is under no obligation to, and expressly disclaims any obligation to, update or alter its forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise. About NTT Research NTT Research opened its offices in July 2019 as a new Silicon Valley startup to conduct basic research and advance technologies that promote positive change for humankind. Currently, three labs are housed at NTT Research facilities in Sunnyvale: the Physics and Informatics (PHI) Lab, the Cryptography and Information Security (CIS) Lab, and the Medical and Health Informatics (MEI) Lab. The organization aims to upgrade reality in three areas: 1) quantum information, neuroscience and photonics; 2) cryptographic and information security; and 3) medical and health informatics. NTT Research is part of NTT, a global technology and business solutions provider with an annual R&D budget of $3.6 billion. About NTT Global Sourcing NTT Global Sourcing was established in November 2018 as a new company specializing in procurement and to bring together the procurement functions of each NTT, Inc. Group company to centralize price negotiations and execute comprehensive agreements with global vendors. CONTACT Sara Steindorf T +314-982-1725 E sara.steindorf@fleishman.com

title: Automatically summarize audio and video files at scale with AI summarization
summary: Learn how AI summarization helps developers and product teams build exciting features that automatically summarize audio and video data.
body_text: The amount of audio and video content available online has been increasing at an exponential rate4a trend supported by recent data shows that 86% of U.S. adults get news from digital devices. This creates both a challenge and an opportunity for product teams building with audio/video. On one hand, there's a tremendous amount of information encoded into audio/video files that can be leveraged to build powerful features and products. On the other hand, it can be difficult for product teams to work with audio/video data in its default state. This guide explores how text summarization transforms audio and video content into actionable insights, covering the technical approaches, business benefits, and practical implementation strategies that leading companies use to build Voice AI-powered summarization at scale. What is text summarization and why it matters for audio and video content Text summarization is an AI process that automatically condenses lengthy text into concise summaries containing the most critical information. For audio and video content, this means converting hours of recordings into actionable insights1key points, decisions, and topicswithout manual review. The real power comes when you combine AI speech-to-text models with summarization capabilities. Instead of just converting audio to text, you're creating structured information that teams can actually usewhether that's generating meeting notes, creating podcast highlights, or extracting customer insights from thousands of support calls. Types of text summarization approaches Two primary AI approaches power text summarization: Extractive summarization: Pulls key sentences directly from original text Ensures factual accuracy by using exact wording Best for compliance monitoring and generating quotes Abstractive summarization: Creates new sentences that capture meaning and context Produces more natural, human-like summaries Ideal for meeting notes, headlines, and content descriptions AssemblyAI's summarization models leverage abstractive techniques to produce more human-like, coherent summaries for any audio or video file. This gives developers the flexibility to choose summary formats that best fit their use case. Text summarization models in action AI technology continues to rapidly advance, making it easier to leverage AI across industries. For example, users can now generate high-quality, realistic images and art with a single text prompt. Transformers have taken the world by storm and opened up the opportunity for Large Language Models (LLMs) that can generate code and write articles . AssemblyAI's AI Summarization models, for example, are built on the same AI technologyTransformersthat are behind most of these advances. The Summarization models are also purpose-built to work well on conversational data (phone calls, zoom meetings, screen recordings, videos, etc.). To demonstrate the power of these models, see the number of examples below: Try AI Summarization on Your Files Upload audio or video and instantly generate headlines, bullet points, or paragraph summaries—no code required. Open Playground Business benefits and ROI of Voice AI summarization AI summarization delivers measurable business returns, and research indicates it can produce an ROI of over 395% for end users across four key areas: Operational efficiency: Automate manual call reviews and QA workflows, with a 2023 study finding that AI assistance increases contact center agent productivity by 14% on average. Business intelligence: Analyze 100% of conversations to identify trends and insights, a practice that is becoming widespread as an industry survey found 76% of companies embed conversation intelligence in over half their customer interactions. User experience: Transform hours of content into scannable highlights Product velocity: Build differentiated features without maintaining AI infrastructure. A survey of tech leaders confirms that partnering with an AI provider allows businesses to focus on innovation and achieve a faster time-to-market. Companies in the conversational intelligence space use summarization to help their customers accelerate QA workflows and reduce time spent on post-call work. When representatives no longer need to manually summarize every interaction, they can handle more conversations and focus on building customer relationships. In fact, research shows AI tools help agents with only two months of tenure perform as well as agents with more than six months of experience. Media platforms use comprehensive summarization to understand content patterns across thousands of hours of recordingsinsights that would be impossible to gather manually. Virtual meeting platforms transform hour-long recordings into scannable highlights that users actually read. Startups like Supernormal and Circleback AI leverage pre-built summarization models to compete with established players. They focus their resources on unique product experiences rather than foundational AI infrastructure. A deep dive into how AssemblyAI's text summarization models work AssemblyAI's text summarization models are fast, scalable, and continuously updated by an in-house team of AI experts to keep it state-of-the-art as new research emerges. These models are accessible through a single API call, making it easy for teams of all sizes to embed the models into their products. For example, you can easily follow along to learn how to request a summary for an audio file using the AssemblyAI Python SDK here. As you'll see in the example, developers have access to customizable summary formats , which are controlled by using the summary_model and summary_type parameters together. This offers developers the flexibility and control they need to generate different types of summaries depending on their use case. For a more detailed guide on how to use the AssemblyAI Python SDK, visit this tutorial . Here is a description of the available summary types AssemblyAI offers: Here is a description of the available summary models and types AssemblyAI offers. For the most up-to-date information, please see the official Summarization documentation . Summary Models The summary model determines the style and tone of the summary. Value When to use Supported summary type informative (default) Best for files with a single speaker, such as presentations or lectures. bullets , bullets_verbose , headline , or paragraph conversational Best for any 2-person conversation, such as customer/agent or interview/interviewee calls. bullets , bullets_verbose , headline , or paragraph catchy Best for creating video, podcast, or media titles. headline , or gist Summary Types The summary type determines both the length and the format of the summary. Value Description bullets (default) A bulleted summary with the most important points. bullets_verbose A longer bullet point list summarizing the entire transcription text. gist A few words summarizing the entire transcription text. headline A single sentence summarizing the entire transcription text. paragraph A single paragraph summarizing the entire transcription text. Use cases for summarization AI text summarization models and AI Summarizers for audio and video help customers across a wide range of industries and use cases, including conversational intelligence, video/media platforms, podcasts, and virtual meeting platforms. Conversational Intelligence A call center application AI summarization can be a powerful addition to conversation intelligence tools and help deliver substantial ROI for end users. Companies like CallSource and Global use summarization to transform their call analytics capabilities. Top benefits of text summarization for conversation intelligence include: Automating manual call review to speed up QA workflows Monitoring all calls for key insights or potential areas of concern Automating notetaking to increase representative and customer engagement Enabling more efficient context sharing between teams Identifying key trends over time Video/Media Platforms A video/media platform AI text summarization can help video and media platforms build tools that distill long educational courses, lectures, media broadcasts, and more into their most essential points for faster consumption. Companies like Veed and Descript use these capabilities to enhance their content creation workflows. Summarization tools can also facilitate easier collaboration between viewers and make it easier for additional conversational intelligence analysis tools to be applied to the summary. Podcasts A podcast platform When integrated into a podcasting platform , text summarization tools can give podcast listeners a quick summary of what the podcast is about before they listen, making the UI more intuitive for users. Platforms like Podchaser leverage these capabilities to improve content discovery. AI summarization can also make podcast episodes more searchable for end users and enhance ad targeting for podcasting platforms by allowing them to serve ads that more closely mirror the listeners' current interests. Virtual Meeting Platforms A virtual meeting platform Reflecting a growing business trend in which virtual meeting use increased to 77% by 2022, virtual meeting platforms and AI voice assistants like Fireflies integrate Voice AI and AI summarization to offer summaries of full meetings, make meeting recordings easier to consume, and readily identify key takeaways and post-call action items. Companies like Supernormal and Circleback AI have built entire businesses around this capability. Some virtual meeting platforms also add shareable video clips that correspond to key moments in the summary. These virtual meeting tools integrate into popular meeting platforms like Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams for ease of use for the end-user. Implementation strategies for audio and video summarization at scale Deploy audio and video summarization in four strategic steps: Define objectives: Identify specific problems like automating meeting notes or creating content previews Ensure accurate transcription: High-quality summaries require precise speech-to-text conversion, and industry research shows that product teams rank quality (58%) and accuracy (47%) as top factors when choosing an AI vendor. Select summary format: Choose between paragraphs, bullet points, headlines, or custom formats Test and scale: Validate with real data, then expand based on user feedback and usage patterns Companies building in production prioritize accuracy in transcriptionif the transcript misses key information, the summary will too. Speech understanding models let you specify summary format with a single parameter, giving you flexibility without complexity. Once you've validated your approach, scaling becomes straightforward. Modern APIs handle millions of hours of audio without requiring infrastructure changes on your end. Scale Summarization in Your Product Access high-quality transcription and customizable summary formats from one API, then deploy to production with confidence.. Get API access Transform your audio and video content with Voice AI summarization The ability to automatically summarize audio and video content is no longer a futuristic conceptit's a practical solution that product teams are deploying today to gain a competitive edge. By turning hours of raw recordings into concise, actionable insights, you can build smarter products, create better user experiences, and operate more efficiently. Leading companies like Whereby and CustomerIQ use text summarization to transform user experiencesturning hours of audio and video into scannable insights that drive faster decision-making. Summarization is an active area of research, and the AssemblyAI AI research team continues to explore these avenues to advance the state-of-the-art. Building this capability is now as simple as integrating an API. If you're ready to unlock the value hidden in your audio and video data, you can start building today. Try our API for free . Frequently asked questions about text summarization How do I choose the right summary type for my application? Choose summary types based on user goals: bullets for meeting overviews, headlines for video titles, and gist for paragraph summaries. Most successful implementations offer multiple options and let users select their preference. Can text summarization handle different languages and accents? Yes, but the quality of the summary is directly tied to the accuracy of the transcript. A highly accurate speech-to-text model that performs well on diverse accents, dialects, and noisy audio is the most important prerequisite for generating high-quality summaries in any language. AssemblyAI's models support multiple languages and handle various accents, ensuring your summaries maintain quality regardless of the speaker. What's the typical implementation timeline for adding summarization to my product? Most teams prototype summarization in hours and deploy production systems within days to weeks, depending on existing infrastructure. Teams with transcription pipelines can add summarization with a simple parameter change. How does summarization handle technical or industry-specific terminology? Modern summarization models are trained on diverse datasets that include technical language from various industries. For highly specialized terminology, the accuracy of the underlying transcription is crucial. To improve the recognition of specific terms, you can use the keyterms_prompt parameter when transcribing with our Universal models. This provides contextual hints to ensure industry-specific terms are correctly captured and included in summaries, making them particularly effective for specialized use cases in healthcare, legal, and technical fields. What's the best way to measure the quality of AI-generated summaries? Measure summary quality through user feedback, A/B testing different formats, and tracking task completion rates. This is critical because abstractive models can hallucinate; in fact, one academic survey concluded that nearly 30% of summaries from abstractive systems didn't align with source document facts. Focus on metrics like time saved and user engagement with summaries. title: Conveyor Reviews, Pricing, and Alternatives (2026)
summary: Conveyor reviews, 2026 pricing, and the main alternatives. Real G2 quotes, what it does well, and where teams switch. Sourced and dated.
body_text: Last updated: July 2026 TL;DR Conveyor is one of the strongest products in security questionnaire automation. G2 reviewers rate it 4 to 5 stars, and the praise is consistent: fast setup, AI that improves as you correct it, and a support team reviewers name unprompted. ‍ Conveyor pricing is public, which is rare in this category. As of July 2026 their pricing page lists a free tier, a Business tier starting at $9,600 per year, and a custom Enterprise tier, on a credit-based model with unlimited seats. ‍ Teams look at Conveyor alternatives for four reasons, all of them raised by Conveyor's own users on G2: portal coverage beyond the browser plugin, parsing of structured spreadsheet fields like dropdowns and mapped cells, permissions deeper than a flat folder structure, and control over the tone of generated answers. ‍ The main Conveyor alternatives are Skypher, SafeBase (now part of Drata), Wolfia, and the RFP-first tools Loopio and Responsive. We make Skypher, so read the comparison with that in mind. Every factual claim here is sourced and dated. ‍ What is Conveyor and how does it work? Conveyor is a security questionnaire automation and trust center platform. It positions itself as "The AI-Native Customer Trust Platform" and automates the customer security review workflow end to end (conveyor.com, as of July 2026). ‍ The product covers three connected jobs. A trust center lets prospects self-serve security documentation without emailing your team. An AI engine drafts questionnaire answers from your knowledge base. A browser extension fills questionnaires inside web portals such as OneTrust and ServiceNow. ‍ Their customer list is strong. As of July 2026 their site names Sumo Logic, Zapier, dbt Labs, Alteryx, Zendesk, Carta, Atlassian, Lucid, Red Canary, Temporal, Loeb & Loeb, Nucleus Security and Nutrient. Anyone telling you Conveyor lacks enterprise traction is not being straight with you. ‍ The metrics they publish as of July 2026: 96% answer accuracy, 98% questionnaire completion rate, 3x capacity increase, and 75% fewer questionnaires reaching the security team. Published case studies include Carta at 83% time reduction, Lucid going from 4 minutes to 22 seconds per question, and Temporal claiming over $100K in annual savings. ‍ For context on the problem all of these tools are solving: across 100,000+ security questions processed through Skypher, 71.2% of questionnaires arrive as Excel, 19.2% through online portals, and 9.6% as Word documents . Format and portal coverage is not a side feature at those proportions. It is most of the job. ‍ Conveyor pricing in 2026 Conveyor publishes pricing openly, which deserves credit. Many vendors in this category, including us, do not. The following is from conveyor.com/pricing as of July 2026 and may have changed since. ‍ Tier Price Includes Free $0 10 Trust Center Credits per month, capped documents and Q&As, no questionnaire automation, no integrations Business "$9,600 starting at /year" Full platform access, unlimited seats, 100 Trust Center Credits, 20 Questionnaire Credits, 10 RFP Projects, volume discounts Enterprise Custom Unlimited seats, pay-per-use with volume discounts, integrations, analytics, enterprise settings, dedicated support ‍ Pricing is usage-based rather than per-seat. Their pricing page states "No per-user fees. No charges for integrations. No nickel-and-dime add-ons." ‍ The unit to understand is the credit. Trust center credits and questionnaire credits are separate allocations, so capacity planning depends on both how many questionnaires you answer and how many organisations view your trust center. One credit equals one organisation accessing your trust center. For teams with steady volume this is easy to forecast. For teams whose trust center traffic spikes during enterprise deal cycles, model it before signing. This is the single most common reason teams search for security questionnaire automation that does not meter per questionnaire or per trust center visit. ‍ Conveyor reviews: what G2 users say The reviews below are from G2, collected between 28 and 31 October 2025. Both praise and criticism are quoted directly rather than paraphrased. What Conveyor users praise Support is the most consistent theme. A daily user calls it "Amazing customer support." Another writes the team "is also super responsive and is always happy to hop on a call to sort out any issues, take feedback, or provide helpful tips." A security consultant lists "Great support - quick and effective" first. Four separate reviewers naming your support team is a real strength, not a marketing line. ‍ Time saved is specific. One daily user reports Conveyor "cut response by half or even less for completing Customer questionnaire." Another says reviews dropped "from several days or weeks to just a couple of days, sometimes even to one day." A third titled their review "Saves Hours." ‍ Setup is fast. "I appreciate how intuitive and straightforward the setup was," writes a reviewer who has run their trust center on it for a year and a half. A security consultant agrees: "Easy to implement - the configuration was very quick and easy." ‍ The AI improves as you correct it. A well-designed feedback loop worth calling out: "when i correct the answer it remembers it for next time - the more you use it, the better it gets and the more it learns. I have seen immense progress in it's answering capabilities in the past 7 months of use." ‍ Completion rates hold up. One reviewer describes submitting "a standard document into the portal and receive more than 90% completion." ‍ Value. A Head of Compliance at a mid-market company: "I believe cost/benefit this is the best value vendor." What Conveyor users ask for These are Conveyor's own customers on G2 describing what they want improved. ‍ Answer tone. The most detailed criticism: "the tone is still not up to par - i do find myself rewriting answers (even if they are correct) so that the sentences flow better, or so that the tone is not so robotic." A separate reviewer wants different behaviour entirely: "I wish it'd bubble up the matching answers and let me decide. I personally don't want AI to write a brand new answer every time." ‍ Portal coverage and plugin friction. "Wider compatibility with the other questionnaire web portal. Plugin does a job but it is little tedious to go to every webpage and upload the questionnaire and then go back to each web page again to apply the answer." ‍ Structured spreadsheet fields. Two reviewers raise this independently. "They need to work on detecting the fields such as drop-downs and its relevant values. In past, I had to manually update the dropdown col. with its relevant values." And from a Head of Compliance: "The process of mapping cells for the AI questionnaire does not appear to function correctly, which results in extra manual work that could be avoided." ‍ Document structure and permissions. "I would like the document folder structure in Conveyor to not be so flat. I would prefer a folder structure that can better accommodate multiple products, with the ability to have subfolders for each product." ‍ Trust center depth. "The trust portal tool does not allow much customization." Another notes that "trust centers from other providers look nicer and psychologically give more of the 'secure and all compliant' feeling." A third raises roadmap concern: "Almost all efforts are focused on AI, RFPs and Automated Questionnaires leaving those who want and signed up for the Trust Center functionality left feeling a bit lost." ‍ Search recall. "I really have to pick up the right keywords to search the relevant content otherwise it says 'No answers'." ‍ Interface density. "Sometimes their UX can feel a bit busy or cluttered." Separately: "I would like the dashboard to be more user-friendly, especially for individuals who aren't involved in the actual security review process." The main Conveyor alternatives in 2026 Five products realistically compete with Conveyor for security questionnaire automation. ‍ Skypher. Questionnaire automation across every format buyers send, with a trust center on the same knowledge base. 40+ portal integrations, answer style control, role-based access control. Adobe, Deel and McKinsey are customers. Best fit for teams with format variety, portal volume, or multi-product permission requirements. Pricing is not public. ‍ SafeBase (Drata). The most mature trust center in the category, acquired by Drata for $250 million in February 2025. Strong access control, buyer analytics, NDA workflow. Questionnaire automation runs through a Chrome extension covering a narrower portal set. Best fit if the trust center is the primary job. Our three-way comparison of SafeBase, Conveyor and Skypher covers this in detail. ‍ Wolfia. Small, fast-moving, built around source citations for every answer. Flat pricing with no questionnaire caps. Best fit for teams whose main concern is verifying where an answer came from. Loopio and Responsive (RFPIO). RFP response platforms that handle security questionnaires as one document type among many. Best fit if RFPs are the larger workload and security questionnaires are secondary. ‍ Vanta and Drata. Compliance automation platforms with questionnaire features attached. Best fit if you need SOC 2 monitoring and questionnaires together. Overkill and expensive if you only need questionnaires. How Skypher compares to Conveyor We make security questionnaire automation software , so this section describes our own product. Four concrete differences rather than a feature list. Portal coverage for online questionnaires Skypher integrates with 40+ questionnaire platforms and pulls questionnaires from portals including OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, Ariba and Coupa into the platform, where you answer them and push responses back in one pass. ‍ This is a different mechanism from a browser extension that assists inside the portal page. Portals are 19.2% of all questionnaires by our data, and the round-trip friction one Conveyor reviewer describes, going to each web page, uploading, then returning to apply answers, is what this design removes. PDF and structured file handling Skypher reads the questionnaire file as it arrives: complex Excel with macros and conditional logic, long Word templates, and PDFs including ones with tables or scans. PDFs go back as PDFs. ‍ This deserves explaining rather than asserting, because "supports PDF" appears on nearly every vendor's feature table and means very little. A real questionnaire is not a list of questions. It has structure: separate fields for the question, the answer and the document reference, Yes/No macros, dropdown menus with defined value sets, conditional logic, multiple tabs. A tool that cannot parse that structure cannot complete the file. You extract questions by hand and paste answers back, which is most of the work. ‍ That is the same underlying issue behind the two G2 comments about dropdown detection and cell mapping. Reading the file is the easy part. Filling it back in correctly is the hard part. Granular permissions and role-based access control Skypher supports role-based access control with granular permissions over who can view, edit and approve what. ‍ For companies with several products, regulated business units, or a review chain running through legal and engineering, permission depth is usually what decides whether a tool can be rolled out beyond one team. It is the area the Conveyor reviewer is gesturing at when asking for subfolders per product instead of a flat structure. Controlling the tone and length of AI answers Skypher gives three answer styles: short answer, precise, and a fully custom prompt written against your own communication guidelines. An agent inside the questionnaire also rephrases individual answers in place, so you can adjust one response without regenerating the rest. ‍ This exists because of the exact complaint the G2 reviewer raises. Security teams give the minimum necessary, since more detail invites more follow-up questions. An answer that is technically correct but three times longer than what your team would send still costs you an edit. Controlling output at generation time removes the edit rather than making it faster. The rest of the stack Skypher runs as an automation layer over tools you already use: questionnaire intake and tracking in Salesforce, review and approval in Slack and Teams, and continuous sync with OneDrive, SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion and your website, so the knowledge base maintains itself as source documents change. Answers carry source citations and confidence scores. Past questionnaires can be set to expire automatically so stale content does not resurface. ‍ Adobe, Deel and McKinsey are customers, across 200+ enterprise customers at 96% accuracy. Adobe went from two weeks to two hours per questionnaire. You can book a demo and send us a real questionnaire to test. Two things we will not claim Accuracy is not a differentiator here. Conveyor publishes 96% answer accuracy. So do we. Anyone presenting that number as a reason to pick one over the other is selling you something. Unlimited seats is not a differentiator either. Both products include unlimited users with no per-seat fee. ‍ Who should choose Conveyor, and who should look at alternatives Choose Conveyor if the trust center is your centre of gravity and questionnaires are the secondary job, your questionnaires arrive mostly through portals their extension already covers, you want public pricing you can budget against without a sales call, and you value support that responds quickly. Their reviewers are consistently happy, and that is not a small thing. ‍ Look at Skypher if questionnaires arrive across many formats including PDFs and structurally complex Excel, a meaningful share come through portals you need covered natively rather than through a plugin, you need permission granularity across products or business units, or your team keeps rewriting technically correct AI answers to match how you actually write. ‍ Look at SafeBase if the trust center is nearly the whole requirement and questionnaire automation is a nice-to-have. ‍ Look at neither if you want compliance monitoring and SOC 2 automation in the same subscription. That is a different category, and buying a questionnaire tool to get it will disappoint you. ‍ Conveyor vs Skypher compared Skypher rows describe our product. Conveyor rows are sourced from conveyor.com and G2 on the dates noted and may have changed since. ‍ Conveyor Skypher Origin Vendor security review platform Questionnaire automation across formats Pricing Public. Business from $9,600/yr, credit-based (Jul 2026) Not public Metering Trust center credits and questionnaire credits Annual volume commitment Seats Unlimited Unlimited Published accuracy 96% 96% Portal handling Browser extension. Users request wider portal compatibility (G2, Oct 2025) 40+ platforms, questionnaires pulled in and pushed back Structured Excel fields Users report dropdown detection and cell mapping gaps (G2, Oct 2025) Macros, dropdowns, conditional logic, multi-tab PDF Supported Supported including tables and scans, returned as PDF Answer tone control Users report rewriting for tone (G2, Oct 2025) Short / precise / custom prompt, plus per-answer rephrase agent Permissions Users request less flat structure (G2, Oct 2025) Role-based access control, granular Trust center Mature. NDA workflow, watermarking, analytics On the same knowledge base as questionnaires Support Repeatedly praised in G2 reviews — ‍ FAQ Is Conveyor a good security questionnaire tool? Yes. G2 reviewers rate Conveyor 4 to 5 stars and consistently report cutting questionnaire turnaround from weeks to days, fast implementation, and responsive support. The most common improvement requests are wider portal coverage, better parsing of structured spreadsheet fields such as dropdowns, deeper permissions, and more control over the tone of generated answers. How much does Conveyor cost? As of July 2026, Conveyor's pricing page listed a free tier with 10 trust center credits per month, a Business tier starting at $9,600 per year including 100 trust center credits and 20 questionnaire credits, and a custom Enterprise tier. Conveyor pricing is credit-based with unlimited seats and no per-user fees. Check their pricing page for current figures. What are the best Conveyor alternatives? The main Conveyor alternatives are Skypher, SafeBase (now part of Drata), Wolfia, and the RFP-first platforms Loopio and Responsive. Skypher fits teams needing broad format and portal coverage, granular role-based permissions, and control over AI answer tone. SafeBase fits trust-center-first teams. Vanta and Drata bundle questionnaire features with compliance automation, which is worth it only if you need both. Which security questionnaire tool integrates with the most vendor portals? Skypher integrates with 40+ questionnaire platforms including OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, Ariba and Coupa, pulling questionnaires into the platform and pushing completed answers back. Conveyor uses a browser extension for portal work, and its G2 reviewers specifically request wider portal compatibility. If most of your questionnaires arrive as portal links rather than files, test portal coverage with your actual portals during evaluation. Does Conveyor handle questionnaires that arrive as PDFs or complex Excel files? Conveyor supports common document formats. Two G2 reviewers in October 2025 reported gaps in structured spreadsheet handling specifically, one on detecting dropdown fields and their value sets, another on cell mapping producing extra manual work. If most of your questionnaires arrive as structurally complex Excel workbooks or PDFs, test with a real customer file during evaluation rather than a clean sample. Our guide to questionnaire formats and where they break covers what to watch for, and our roundup of questionnaire automation tools compares the wider field.

title: The promise – and limitations – of AI in JCA PICO planning for pharmas and medtechs
summary: Developing robust PICO assumptions requires input from a variety of sources. AI can help teams quickly identify, retrieve and summarize volumes of information.
body_text: The central challenge of Joint Clinical Assessment (JCA) is building a dossier before knowing precisely what evidence will be requested by the HTA Coordination Group – effectively, preparing an answer to a question that has not yet been asked. If outcomes aligned with JCA-defined PICO components (Problem or Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) are not anticipated early, health technology developers (HTDs) can face a last-minute rush to generate evidence within a short submission window. To reduce this risk, HTDs are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve both the speed and quality of PICO planning. AI can be useful for rapidly synthesizing information, and is effective at surfacing precedent, but it cannot determine what will be considered decision-relevant in a future JCA. Translating these insights into robust and defensible PICO assumptions requires expert interpretation, informed by a deep understanding of how the reimbursement landscape is evolving. Here, we look at some of the ways it can support PICO planning, as well as its limitations. How Clarivate leverages AI to strengthen PICO planning Developing robust PICO assumptions requires input from a variety of sources, including HTA decisions, JCA documentation, and clinical guidelines. However, identifying and generating this information via traditional desk research can be a time-consuming and resource-intensive process. AI can help teams quickly identify, retrieve, and summarize large volumes of information, including: Prior HTA assessments and clinical guidelines in the indication, highlighting relevant comparators and outcomes of interest Clinical trial data for the product of interest and key competitors Methodological guidance and scoping documents from the HTA Coordination Group outlining requirements for dossier development However, identifying relevant data is only the first step. Filtering and interpreting what that evidence means for PICO planning requires the experience and judgement of seasoned systematic review specialists and HTA experts who help contextualise findings, ensure alignment with reimbursement expectations and validate assumptions. A deep understanding of policy and HTA evidence requirements is important for predicting how decision-makers may prioritize comparators and endpoints within the JCA framework. Together, these perspectives help ensure PICO assumptions are not only grounded in high-quality evidence but are also relevant to how decisions will be made in practice. Early PICO planning can also be informed by primary research with appropriate clinicians and payers. Insights from primary research can inform clear recommendations that align with HTA expectations. For example, obtaining clinicians’ perspectives on real-world practice, including evolving standards of care, treatment pathways, unmet need and clinically meaningful outcomes, can provide important context that cannot be derived from published evidence alone. This is important because JCA assessments are expected to focus on outcomes considered clinically meaningful in practice, not simply those captured in existing evidence. Ultimately, while AI can streamline evidence gathering and highlight historical precedent, human expertise is needed to interpret these insights, along with inputs from clinicians and payers, and apply them to the current landscape. Clarivate understands the importance of PICO readiness Clarivate’s JCA and HTA Centre of Excellence brings together multidisciplinary teams across HTA, evidence generation and medical writing, with experience spanning more than 250 global HTA submissions and over 500 global value dossiers. This experience includes pan-European joint HTA programs, including successful BeNeLuxA initiative submissions. Our consultants work closely with clients from early development through submission to define, stress-test, and refine PICO assumptions. The JCA strategies we present to clients combine evidence review, stakeholder input, and cross-country HTA insight to anticipate likely submission requirements and reduce downstream risk. We integrate expertise from clinicians and payers into PICO planning, ensuring assumptions are grounded in real-world practice and aligned with evolving decision drivers. This allows us to identify potential misalignment early and proactively address evidence gaps before they become critical. Our systematic review specialists and HTA consultants are supported by proprietary AI tools that help accelerate and enhance evidence synthesis. Importantly, these tools are embedded within expert-led workflows, ensuring outputs are comprehensive, interpretable and defensible. When used together, these capabilities help teams prepare more effectively for JCA, respond more quickly to unexpected PICO requests and identify potential evidence gaps earlier in the process. title: 13 Proven Best Practices for Spend Management Optimisation for Fast-Growing Businesses

body_text: As a business owner, you understand that every rupee spent impacts your company's profitability. But are you truly in control of where and how your money flows? Without a comprehensive spend management strategy, it's easy to lose track of expenditures, leading to inefficiencies and missed opportunities for cost savings. In fact, the average business wastes around 30% of its SaaS spend due to underutilised subscriptions and redundant tools. This is just one example of how a lack of visibility and control can result in financial leakage. Hence, the growing importance of spend management optimisation among businesses. However, before you scramble to track and optimise every expense to drive business growth, ask yourself, “ Is this the right approach? ” We understand that while spend management optimisation is important, it’s not always easy to carry out. That’s why we’re here to help you with it. In this comprehensive article, we will introduce you to some of the most important best practices for spend management optimisation. We’ll also offer practical tips for improving your company's spending strategy and financial health. TL;DR (Key Takeaways) Spend management optimisation helps your business improve efficiency, reduce waste, and make smarter, data-driven decisions. Consolidate spend data, track spending patterns, categorise expenses, and automate workflows to streamline your procurement process. Leverage modern procurement tech and spend management software, like Kodo, for efficiency, accuracy, and real-time insights. Spend management optimisation is an ongoing process, requiring regular audits, reviews, and adjustments to stay ahead. What is Spend Management? Spend management is the strategic process of controlling, tracking, and optimising all of your company’s expenditures. It involves understanding how money is spent across departments and categories. Moreover, it strategically helps manage this spend to reduce waste, negotiate better deals, and align purchases with your business’s financial goals. Spend management encompasses everything from procurement and supplier relationships to internal controls and purchasing procedures. It enables your business to track, control, and optimise its financial resources in a way that maximises value and minimises inefficiencies. Benefits of Spend Management Proper spend management is crucial since it helps your business align its spending with its long-term goals. With complete visibility over where your money is going, you can ensure that every rupee spent contributes to building your business. Therefore, implementing an effective spend management strategy offers numerous advantages: Cost Reduction : By tracking and managing expenditures, you can identify areas where your company is overspending and reduce unnecessary costs. Better Budgeting and Forecasting : With clear visibility into spend patterns, you can ensure that expenditures stay within budget and plan more accurately for future expenses. Improved Supplier Relationships : Effective procurement and spend management allow your business to negotiate better prices and terms with suppliers. Increased Operational Efficiency : Streamlining procurement and payment processes saves time and reduces manual errors, ensuring smooth operations. Better Compliance and Transparency : A well-defined spend management process promotes transparency, accountability, and adherence to financial regulations. Having understood what spend management exactly is, it’s time for you to discover why it’s important to optimise this process. What is Spend Management Optimisation? Spend management optimisation takes the basic principles of spend management to the next level. It is the strategic process of refining and enhancing how your business manages its expenditures. This means not just tracking and controlling, but actively seeking opportunities to reduce costs and improve efficiency. Unlike traditional spend management, which may focus solely on cost control, spend management optimisation adopts a holistic view. It leverages data analytics, automation, and strategic sourcing to transform spending into a competitive advantage. This allows you to make smarter purchasing decisions, improve financial performance, and gain a competitive edge. Some of the crucial objectives of spend management optimisation are: Maximising Value : Ensuring that every rupee spent contributes to your business’s goals. Now that you understand why spend management optimisation is so important for your business, let’s discuss some strategies to implement it in your company. 13 Key Best Practices for Spend Management Optimisation To truly optimise your spend management, it's crucial to adopt a set of best practices that will streamline your financial processes and drive better decision-making. These strategies also enable you to control costs and unlock opportunities for growth and efficiency. Here are the most important best practices you must understand to fine-tune the spend management approach for your business. Consolidate All Spend Data To optimise your spend management, start by consolidating all your spending data in a single, accessible location. This gives you a clear, unified view of where your money is going. Even recent reports state that 74% of business owners agree that siloed data hampers their business performance. With consolidated visibility, you can make informed decisions, identify patterns, and spot inefficiencies. It’s essential for tracking expenses across departments, streamlining processes, and avoiding duplicated efforts. Categorise and Classify Expenses Accurately Next, properly categorise and classify your expenses to identify hidden cost-saving opportunities. This makes it easier to spot areas of excessive spending and take corrective action for better cost control. Pro Tip : Regularly update your classification systems to account for new categories, such as emerging technologies or new operational requirements. Track and Analyse Spending Patterns Tracking and analysing your spending patterns regularly will help you understand where your business is overspending or underutilising resources. By identifying trends, you can optimise purchasing decisions and avoid budget overruns. Use Historical Spend Data to Forecast Budgets Use your historical spending data to forecast future budgets more accurately. This data-driven approach ensures that your budgets reflect actual business needs rather than assumptions. This leads to more effective planning and helps you avoid unexpected expenses. Strategic Supplier Sourcing and Relationship Management Building strong relationships with your suppliers is key to spend management optimisation. Manage your supplier relationships strategically to negotiate better pricing, improved payment terms, and more favourable delivery schedules. It’s important to focus on long-term partnerships instead of transactional ones to secure better value from your suppliers and enhance your supply chain’s stability. Optimise and Review Vendor Contracts Frequently Regularly review and optimise your vendor contracts to ensure you’re getting the best deal possible. Conduct Regular Reviews and Audits Spend management optimisation is an ongoing process. Conduct regular reviews and audits to assess the effectiveness of your current policies and identify areas for improvement. Additionally, it helps you refine processes, cut costs, and maximise value as your business evolves. With these best practices, you’ll be well on your way to optimising the spend management processes in your business. Armed with this clear understanding of the best practices, let’s take a look at how Kodo can support your spend management journey. title: What Is Multi-Agent Orchestration? The Developer's Guide
summary: How multi-agent orchestration works, why parallel agent execution matters, and what engineering teams should evaluate before adopting it.
body_text: The Context Window Problem: Why Single-Agent AI Development Hits a Ceiling Context windows limit how much of a codebase an AI agent can reason about in a single turn. This constraint shapes how developers work with AI assistants, particularly in larger projects where relevant context can exceed available capacity. Git worktree isolation helps address this by giving each agent a separate working directory. Instead of forcing one agent to absorb the entire problem, teams can break work into bounded tasks and run them in parallel while a coordinating agent tracks the broader architecture. Git worktree allows multiple working trees attached to the same repository, which Proliferate uses to keep agent contexts isolated and focused. Orchestration Patterns: From Fan-Out to Peer Review How agents coordinate determines whether a multi-agent system speeds work up or just adds overhead. Fan-Out / Fan-In distributes a task across multiple agents working in parallel on separate components, then aggregates the results for integration. Pipeline chains agents sequentially, where each agent's output feeds the next as input. Proliferate's plan/code/review agents support this pattern, allowing teams to enforce handoffs like requirements validated before implementation or tests passing before deployment. Supervisor uses a hierarchical control structure where an orchestrator agent directs subagents, allocates tasks dynamically, and manages dependencies. Peer Review runs multiple agents in parallel on the same task, then compares outputs to surface consensus and discrepancies. A supervisor might fan out across components, with each component following a plan-code-review pipeline and peer review validating the critical outputs.
